extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in television/entertainment industry news (SNL fans, industry observers, general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and explaining rationale behind casting changes and personnel decisions for a long-running televised sketch comedy show (here, SNL). Covers reasons for non-renewal, bringing in new cast, guest casting, and how controversy or chemistry can factor in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change is the lifeblood of the show
rubrics_metrics.description: "Change is the lifeblood of the show; it always has been. And you have to keep bringing new people in."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lorne Michaels states turnover and fresh talent are an explicit, ongoing standard for SNL; bringing new people in is cited as a reason for letting established cast members go even if they performed well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts and non-renewal as personnel mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials may choose not to renew existing cast contracts rather than give a specific public reason for departures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Killam and Pharoah had a year left on their contracts but were not returning; no exact reason was revealed other than contracts would not be renewed — implying contractual decisions are a tool for reshaping cast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past performance and service to the show
rubrics_metrics.description: "I think they were great, and they did wonderful work when they were with us...They served the show well, and are two people I really care about."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Michaels emphasizes that good performance and personal regard do not guarantee retention; service and quality are acknowledged but balanced against broader show needs like change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-show prospects factor into decisions or reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving SNL can lead to other opportunities (e.g., cast members landing pilots or series elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites both performers being cast in new Showtime pilots, suggesting that the potential for cast members' future success is recognized and can temper concern about departures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting can originate from peer suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: "She said, 'You know who would be a great Trump is Alec!'…Slowly, the idea grew on me." (Tina Fey suggested Alec Baldwin for Trump.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guest or high-profile casting choices may arise from ideas suggested by other performers or creatives; such suggestions can influence recruitment of notable talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer chemistry matters in casting choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Michaels thought Alec Baldwin "would be great with Kate [McKinnon] (who portrays Hillary Clinton)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations about how a performer pairs with current cast (chemistry, complementary portrayals) are part of the casting rationale for recurring guest roles or character pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and controversy are relevant to personnel context
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes the addition of the first Latina comedian (Melissa Villaseñor) and references controversy around her removed tweets deemed racist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting and personnel narratives include attention to diversity milestones and public controversies; these elements can influence perception and discussion of casting decisions even if not stated as the official reason for hires or departures.
